title: Seerah
description: Little Muslim → Mid. Short questions for children who know the first basics of the Prophet’s ﷺ life. Covers his shepherd work, the call at Safa, the Night Journey, the prescribing of daily prayers, the qiblah change, Hijrah preparations, the Ansar, Quba, Hudaybiyyah, community work and caring everyday conduct. Uses familiar learning and home situations to connect authentic accounts with simple lessons. An adult may read questions aloud or explain unfamiliar words. All questions are Mid level within the Kids audience.
levelMethod: Mid describes the knowledge and understanding needed across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Builds on introductory Seerah through familiar events, simple relationships, basic historical distinctions and straightforward lessons for everyday life. No obscure dates, specialist historical debates or memorization of reference numbers is required. Level is editorial guidance, not calibrated with children's reading or response data. Quiz performance describes learning needs, not a child's faith or worth.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages and authentic hadith reports checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original child-friendly educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Historical events and relationships are kept distinct from present-day illustrations. The mosque-building account describes the Prophet being with the builders and praying for them; the trench account separately describes him carrying earth. Patience and mercy are not presented as requiring children to tolerate physical aggression or ongoing harm. Classroom comparisons with Hudaybiyyah do not reproduce the treaty's terms or turn every agreement into a religious requirement. Receiving gifts does not create an instruction to accept unsafe gifts or spend beyond a family's means. The account of Umamah is used for family relationships and tenderness, not as a full guide to prayer procedure. No question asks children to judge another person's faith or worth. This is not independent scholarly approval or a completed review with children.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: Which work did the Prophet ﷺ say he had done for people in Makkah?

options.text: Caring for their sheep
Ruling their empire
Building their ships
Leading their royal court

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ said he had cared for sheep belonging to people in Makkah. His life included useful, ordinary work.

questions.question: Where did the Prophet ﷺ gather people when calling his near relatives to hear his warning?

options.text: Quba
Safa
Mina
Arafat

questions.explanation: The report describes him calling the clans of Quraysh together at Safa. He publicly delivered an important warning to his people.

questions.question: Which two mosques are connected by the Prophet's ﷺ Night Journey in the Quran?

options.text: The Prophet's Mosque and Quba Mosque
Quba Mosque and Al-Masjid al-Haram
Al-Masjid al-Haram and Al-Masjid al-Aqsa
Al-Masjid al-Aqsa and Quba Mosque

questions.explanation: The Quran describes Allah taking His servant by night from Al-Masjid al-Haram to Al-Masjid al-Aqsa to show him signs.

questions.question: How many daily prayers remained prescribed in the account of the Prophet's ﷺ heavenly journey?

options.text: Two
Three
Seven
Five

questions.explanation: The authentic account describes the prayers being reduced until five remained. This event connects daily salah with the Prophet's ﷺ heavenly journey.

questions.question: After the qiblah changed in Madinah, which direction did the Prophet ﷺ face in prayer?

options.text: Toward the Kaaba in Makkah
Toward whichever landmark was nearest
Toward the sunrise every day
Toward a different city each week

questions.explanation: The report describes the change from facing Jerusalem to facing the Kaaba. The companions followed the new direction when they learned of it.

questions.question: Who prepared journey food for the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr before their migration to Madinah?

options.text: Hafsah, Umar's daughter
Asma, Abu Bakr's daughter
Umm Salamah
Safiyyah

questions.explanation: Asma described preparing food for their journey. Her practical help was part of the preparations for the Hijrah.

questions.question: What practical help did the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr arrange for their Hijrah route?

options.text: A competition for the fastest runner
A crowd to announce their route
An expert guide
A royal parade

questions.explanation: They employed a skilled guide whom they trusted. The journey included careful planning and practical help.

questions.question: Which mosque did the Prophet ﷺ regularly visit, sometimes walking and sometimes riding?

options.text: A mosque in a different country every week
A mosque built only after his lifetime
A mosque chosen by drawing lots each visit
Quba Mosque

questions.explanation: The report describes his regular visits to Quba Mosque. It records visits both on foot and while riding.

questions.question: What were the believers in Madinah who welcomed and helped the emigrants called?

options.text: The Ansar
The emigrants themselves
The rulers of Rome
The travelers of Quraysh who opposed them

questions.explanation: The Ansar were the helpers in Madinah. The Quran praises their love for the emigrants and their generous care for them.

questions.question: What kind of agreement did the Prophet ﷺ conclude with Quraysh at Hudaybiyyah?

options.text: A school timetable
A peace treaty
A promise to stop worshipping Allah
A plan to replace the Quran

questions.explanation: The authentic account describes a negotiated peace treaty. Hudaybiyyah is an important event in the Prophet's ﷺ life.

questions.question: What did the Prophet ﷺ do while he was with the companions building the mosque in Madinah?

options.text: Told them their work had no value
Said worship had no place in Madinah
Asked Allah to forgive the helpers and emigrants
Forbade them from working together

questions.explanation: The report describes the Prophet ﷺ with the builders, praying for the Ansar and emigrants. Their community work was accompanied by remembrance of Allah.

questions.question: During the work at the trench, what did the Prophet ﷺ himself help carry?

options.text: Royal furniture
Goods for a private palace
Prizes for a race
Earth

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ helped carry earth during the trench work. He shared the effort and called upon Allah for help.

questions.question: After painful rejection, what did the Prophet ﷺ hope for when offered punishment for the people?

options.text: That their descendants would worship Allah alone
That nobody in their families could ever improve
That revenge would be his only goal
That all future generations would lose hope

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ chose a merciful response and expressed hope for future believers. His grief did not become a wish for endless revenge.

questions.question: How did the Prophet ﷺ respond when a man roughly pulled his cloak and demanded wealth?

options.text: He ordered everyone to insult the man's family
He smiled and ordered that the man receive something
He encouraged people to copy the rough behavior
He demanded that every child surrender their belongings

questions.explanation: The report shows remarkable patience and generosity. It does not make rough grabbing good manners.

questions.question: When a visitor urinated in the mosque, what did the Prophet ﷺ instruct the people to do?

options.text: Beat him to teach the whole crowd a lesson
Leave the place dirty forever
Leave him and have water poured over the place
Make his mistake into a public joke

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ prevented a harsh response and directed the cleaning. He taught making things easier rather than unnecessarily difficult.

questions.question: What small interest of the child Abu Umayr did the Prophet ﷺ ask about?

options.text: His royal palace
His trading fleet
His army
His little bird

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ spoke warmly to the child about his little bird. A child's small interests were not beneath his attention.

questions.question: Which granddaughter did the Prophet ﷺ carry during prayer in this report?

options.text: Umamah
Aishah
Khadijah
Hafsah

questions.explanation: Umamah was the daughter of his daughter Zaynab. The report describes him carrying her and putting her down when prostrating.

questions.question: How did Aishah describe the Prophet's ﷺ practice with gifts?

options.text: He always mocked the giver
He accepted gifts and gave something in return
He treated every gift as permission to boast
He demanded that every gift be expensive

questions.explanation: Aishah reported that he accepted gifts and reciprocated. His example shows gracious receiving and giving.

questions.question: What did Aishah connect with the Prophet's ﷺ character when asked about it?

options.text: A collection of royal customs
A desire to win popularity at any cost
The Quran
A habit of ignoring Allah's guidance

questions.explanation: Aishah described his character through the Quran. His life showed its guidance in practice, rather than separating knowledge from conduct.

questions.question: In his Hajj sermon, what did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize about people's lives, belongings and honor?

options.text: They matter only when a person is wealthy
They may be harmed for entertainment
They have no importance outside a ceremony
They must be respected and protected

questions.explanation: The sermon strongly emphasized the protection of life, property and honor. These were serious responsibilities, not passing words.

questions.question: Does the Prophet's ﷺ work as a shepherd suggest honest everyday work is shameful?

options.text: No, his life included useful ordinary work
Yes, only famous people deserve respect
Yes, caring for animals has no value
No, because he said he never worked

questions.explanation: The report reminds us that the Prophet ﷺ did useful work. We should not look down on a person for an honest occupation.

questions.question: What makes the gathering at Safa important in the Prophet's ﷺ life story?

options.text: He was choosing a new king for Rome
He openly called his people to hear his warning
He announced that revelation had never come
He was arranging a sports tournament

questions.explanation: The gathering was part of delivering his message publicly. It was a serious call to his people, not an entertainment event.

questions.question: Is the Night Journey described in the Quran the same event as the Hijrah to Madinah?

options.text: Yes, both names mean moving to Madinah
Yes, Al-Aqsa is another name for Madinah
No, the journeys have different destinations and meanings
No, because the Quran mentions no Night Journey

questions.explanation: The Night Journey connects Al-Masjid al-Haram with Al-Masjid al-Aqsa. It is different from the migration to Madinah.

questions.question: Which link between Seerah and daily worship appears in the heavenly journey account?

options.text: The rule that daily prayer is only for travelers
The idea that every person chooses a different number
The claim that prayer began as a classroom game
The prescribing of the five daily prayers

questions.explanation: The account connects the five daily prayers with the heavenly journey. Learning Seerah can also explain the history of familiar worship.

questions.question: In the account of the qiblah change, what did companions do when informed of the new direction?

options.text: Turned toward the Kaaba
Chose a direction by guessing
Decided that prayer no longer mattered
Made every person face a different direction

questions.explanation: The companions responded to the report of the changed qiblah. The account shows them following the newly taught direction.

questions.question: What does Asma's role in preparing the journey food show?

options.text: Only the people traveling can ever help
Practical support can contribute to an important effort
Food preparation can never be useful
Women had no part in supporting the Hijrah

questions.explanation: Asma's contribution was practical and valuable. Preparing what travelers needed was part of supporting the journey.

questions.question: Does arranging a guide for the Hijrah conflict with trusting Allah?

options.text: Yes, trust means rejecting every skilled helper
Yes, planning a route is always wrong
No, the Prophet ﷺ used trustworthy practical help
No, because the Prophet ﷺ never made any plans

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ arranged skilled help for the journey. Trust in Allah and sensible preparation can go together.

questions.question: What does the report about walking or riding to Quba describe?

options.text: A rule that everyone must own a riding animal
A journey to a different continent
A visit that happened only after his lifetime
The Prophet's ﷺ visits to that mosque

questions.explanation: The report records a practice from his life. Walking and riding are both mentioned; it does not require every person to own a mount.

questions.question: Which attitude matches the Quran's praise of the Ansar toward the emigrants?

options.text: Loving welcome and generous support
Jealousy whenever another person received help
Treating newcomers as people without dignity
Refusing to care about another believer's needs

questions.explanation: The Quran praises the helpers' love and generosity. Their care for newcomers was more than simply knowing their names.

questions.question: What does the Hudaybiyyah account show about addressing conflict?

options.text: Every disagreement must become a fight
Negotiation and agreement can be part of a solution
Listening to the other side is always forbidden
Peaceful agreements have no place in Seerah

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ concluded an agreement through negotiation. This event shows that resolving conflict need not mean escalating it.

questions.question: What does the Prophet's ﷺ prayer for the mosque builders show?

options.text: That only wealthy helpers were worth remembering
That practical work and worship could never meet
Appreciation for those serving the community
That the builders should compete in insulting one another

questions.explanation: He prayed for the Ansar and emigrants while with them. Community effort and remembrance of Allah belonged together.

questions.question: Did the Prophet ﷺ consider himself too important to share the trench work?

options.text: Yes, helping was beneath his dignity
Yes, only unknown people could do useful work
No, because no work was done at the trench
No, he helped carry earth himself

questions.explanation: His participation shows leadership through shared effort. He did not leave every difficult task to others.

questions.question: Which lesson fits the Prophet's ﷺ hope after painful rejection?

options.text: People and future generations can still turn toward good
A person's family must be hated forever
Revenge is the only response to disappointment
One harsh encounter proves nobody can ever improve

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ expressed hope instead of choosing destruction. We can learn mercy without pretending that hurtful treatment is acceptable.

questions.question: Does the Prophet's ﷺ generous response make pulling someone's clothing an acceptable way to ask?

options.text: Yes, grabbing is the best way to receive help
No, his patience does not make the roughness right
Yes, force always makes a request polite
No, but insulting the giver would be better

questions.explanation: The report praises his patience and generosity. It does not teach us to demand help through force.

questions.question: What does the visitor's mosque incident show about gentleness and correcting a problem?

options.text: Gentleness requires leaving every place dirty
Correction is only useful when someone is humiliated
A problem can be corrected without a cruel response
Cleaning becomes wrong if it is done calmly

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ directed cleaning while preventing harshness. Dealing with a mistake and treating a person gently can happen together.

questions.question: Why is the Prophet's ﷺ conversation about Abu Umayr's bird meaningful?

options.text: It proves children's interests never matter
It says only adults deserve conversation
It means every child must keep the same pet
It shows warm attention to a child's world

questions.explanation: The child received kind attention about something familiar to him. The report does not require every family to keep a bird.

questions.question: How was Umamah related to the Prophet ﷺ?

options.text: She was his daughter's daughter
She was his mother
She was his wife
She was his aunt

questions.explanation: Umamah was Zaynab's daughter and the Prophet's ﷺ granddaughter. The report also shows his tenderness toward her.

questions.question: Which description matches the report about the Prophet's ﷺ gifts?

options.text: Demanding expensive gifts before treating people kindly
Receiving graciously and responding with giving
Using gifts as an excuse to insult the giver
Treating every gift as a competition for wealth

questions.explanation: The report describes accepting gifts and giving in return. This example is about gracious conduct, not turning kindness into a contest.

questions.question: Does Aishah's description mean the Prophet ﷺ was literally a physical book?

options.text: Yes, he was made from pages
Yes, he had no human life
No, it describes his conduct reflecting Quranic guidance
No, because she said the Quran had no guidance

questions.explanation: Aishah was describing character, not physical form. The meaning is that Quranic guidance was reflected in how he lived.

questions.question: Does the sermon about life, property and honor mean mistreating someone is only a problem during Hajj?

options.text: Yes, people's belongings matter only during Hajj
Yes, harm is acceptable on ordinary school days
No, but only popular people's dignity matters
No, its teaching concerns respect beyond the gathering too

questions.explanation: The sermon uses the sacred occasion to emphasize people's rights. Its lesson is not limited to those listening at that moment.

questions.question: A classmate mocks someone for tending animals. Remembering the Prophet's ﷺ work, what is a better response?

options.text: Explain that honest useful work deserves respect
Join in because simple work is shameful
Claim only rich people's work matters
Say the Prophet ﷺ never cared for sheep

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ himself had tended sheep. A person's honest work is not a reason to mock them.

questions.question: Your class labels an event card, "The Prophet ﷺ publicly calls his people together." Which place fits this report?

options.text: Quba
Safa
Mina
Arafat

questions.explanation: The report places this gathering at Safa. Learning the event helps us connect a familiar place with his public message.

questions.question: Sara makes a route card for the Night Journey. Which destination belongs after Al-Masjid al-Haram?

options.text: Quba Mosque
The Prophet's Mosque in Madinah
Al-Masjid al-Aqsa
A school in Makkah

questions.explanation: The Quran names Al-Masjid al-Aqsa as the destination in this journey. Sara should keep it separate from the Hijrah route.

questions.question: A learning card links the heavenly journey with daily salah. Which number of prescribed daily prayers belongs on it?

options.text: Two
Three
Seven
Five

questions.explanation: The report describes five daily prayers remaining prescribed. The card should connect this familiar worship with the correct Seerah event.

questions.question: Yusuf draws a timeline of prayer directions after the Hijrah. Which order matches the report?

options.text: Jerusalem, then the Kaaba
The Kaaba, then the sunrise
Quba, then a different city every week
A different direction for every person

questions.explanation: The report describes the Prophet ﷺ facing Jerusalem before the change to the Kaaba. Yusuf's timeline should preserve that order.

questions.question: After learning Asma's role, Maryam wants to help her family prepare for a trip. Which safe task fits the lesson?

options.text: Hide the supplies to make everyone worry
Help pack food with a parent's guidance
Take money from someone else's bag
Refuse to help because she is not driving

questions.explanation: Asma helped through practical preparation. Maryam can contribute through an age-appropriate task guided by her parent.

questions.question: Before a family journey, Adam says planning shows no trust in Allah. What would the Hijrah guide account help explain?

options.text: The Prophet ﷺ rejected every form of guidance
No one ever helped with the route
The Prophet ﷺ used careful planning and skilled help
Trust requires traveling without knowing where we are going

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr arranged a trusted expert guide. Sensible preparation does not cancel reliance on Allah.

questions.question: A worksheet asks which mosque the Prophet ﷺ visited regularly on foot or riding. Which name should Hana write?

options.text: A mosque built centuries later
A different unnamed mosque every week
A mosque chosen through a game
Quba Mosque

questions.explanation: Quba is named in the authentic report. Hana can connect the place with the practice described in his life.

questions.question: A new pupil arrives after moving to your town. Which welcome reflects the generosity shown by the Ansar?

options.text: Help them feel included and share permitted supplies
Mock them for being new
Hide the information they need
Insist that newcomers deserve no help

questions.explanation: The Ansar's care for emigrants offers a lesson in welcoming others. A classroom welcome is an illustration, not the historical Hijrah itself.

questions.question: Two classmates disagree over a shared activity. What approach reflects a simple lesson from Hudaybiyyah?

options.text: Assume fighting is the only possible solution
Seek a calm agreement with a teacher's guidance
Refuse to listen to any explanation
Make threats until the other child cries

questions.explanation: The historical treaty shows negotiation as part of resolving conflict. A teacher can help children seek a fair, safe agreement.

questions.question: Classmates help arrange a prayer space with a teacher. Which response reflects appreciation for community helpers?

options.text: Call their help worthless
Claim helpers should never be remembered
Recognize their effort and make dua for them
Turn their work into a reason to mock them

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ prayed for the helpers while with the mosque builders. We can appreciate those who serve a good purpose.

questions.question: Your group has a safe classroom task to finish. Which choice reflects the Prophet's ﷺ shared effort at the trench?

options.text: Say helping is beneath your importance
Take the credit without doing any work
Make the smallest child do every task
Do your suitable share instead of leaving everything to others

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ took part in the trench work. A child can learn cooperation through safe tasks suited to their ability.

questions.question: After a disagreement, Ali wishes harm on his friend's whole family. What response reflects the Prophet's ﷺ mercy?

options.text: Avoid revenge and hope they choose what is good
Blame every relative for the disagreement
Plan to humiliate the family forever
Decide no one in that family can ever improve

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ showed hope after painful rejection. Ali can reject revenge and seek adult help if the disagreement involves ongoing harm.

questions.question: A classmate speaks rudely when asking for a pencil. Which response reflects patience while keeping sensible boundaries?

options.text: Pull their clothing to get revenge
Reply calmly and ask them to speak respectfully
Insult their family in front of everyone
Assume rude demands must always be obeyed

questions.explanation: The Prophet's ﷺ patient response can inspire calm conduct. It does not require accepting rough treatment; seek help if someone becomes physically aggressive.

questions.question: A younger child spills water during a lesson. Which response applies gentleness while fixing a problem?

options.text: Make everyone laugh at the child
Leave the spill so someone slips
Get suitable help to clean without humiliating the child
Shout that the child can never improve

questions.explanation: This is a classroom illustration of gentle correction, not the same incident. Fix the problem safely without turning a mistake into humiliation.

questions.question: A younger sibling wants to tell you about a small interest. Which response follows the Prophet's ﷺ warm attention to children?

options.text: Say only adults deserve to be heard
Mock them for caring about something small
Ignore them only to show you are older
Listen kindly instead of dismissing them as unimportant

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ gave kind attention to Abu Umayr's interest. Listening warmly can help a younger child feel valued.

questions.question: A family-tree activity places Umamah below Zaynab, the Prophet's ﷺ daughter. What is Umamah's relationship to him?

options.text: Granddaughter
Mother
Wife
Aunt

questions.explanation: Umamah was the daughter of Zaynab. That makes her the Prophet's ﷺ granddaughter, as the report explains.

questions.question: With your parent's permission, a friend gives you a small gift. Which response reflects gracious receiving and giving?

options.text: Mock the gift because it is inexpensive
Receive it kindly and consider a suitable gift in return
Demand a bigger one before speaking politely
Turn it into a competition over whose family is richer

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ accepted gifts and reciprocated. Let a parent guide any gift in return; kindness need not become an expensive contest.

questions.question: You learn Aishah's description of the Prophet's ﷺ character. What is a useful goal for your own Quran learning?

options.text: Memorize facts while refusing every good change
Use what you know only to belittle classmates
Try to let its guidance improve your behavior
Decide reading and conduct must never connect

questions.explanation: His character reflected Quranic guidance. A learner can aim to connect understanding with better everyday choices.

questions.question: A friend suggests damaging another child's belongings for fun. Which response follows the Hajj sermon's lesson about rights?

options.text: Agree because it is only a school day
Join in if the child is unpopular
Claim belongings deserve respect only during Hajj
Refuse and respect the child's belongings and dignity

questions.explanation: The sermon strongly protects people's rights. A child's belongings and dignity should not become targets for entertainment or revenge.
